CIM 2026 — XXV Colloquio di Informatica Musicale L'Aquila · 14 October 2026

Armillaria

A Minimal Networked System for Real-Time Performance Conduction
Bruno Surace · Andrea Valle CIRMA · StudiUm · Università di Torino
01

Notation
& conduction

the idea

A conductor — the kybernete — types plain-text instructions that appear instantly on musicians' browsers over a local WiFi network. No apps, no accounts, no proprietary hardware.

The name borrows from Armillaria, the honey fungus genus whose mycelium spreads in vast underground networks — invisible at the surface, connecting many nodes without a centre.

Four axes of notation

  • Type — standard, graphic, or textual
  • Orientation — representational or prescriptive
  • Timing — outside-time or in-time
  • Addressee — machine, or human

live coding, displaced

A live coder who types freq = 440 produces a deterministic result; a kybernete who types pianissimo produces as many results as there are musicians reading it.
Armillaria — textual, prescriptive, in-time, human-addressed

02

System
architecture

fig. Signal flow for Nickelodeon digitale — text, video and audio paths · code: github.com/vanderaalle/armillaria
relay → all receivers, unfiltered
{"text": "Saxophone: pianissimo, long", "from": "Kybernete"}
same envelope whether "text" is broadcast or addressed to one name — the server doesn't parse it
ack → originating sender
{"type": "ack", "text": "..."}
+ "empty": true if no receivers are currently connected
server

Envelope & acknowledgement

A Python websockets server relays every sender's message to every receiver, wrapped with the sender's identity. It never reads or filters the text — not even to tell a broadcast from a message addressed to one musician. Every relay also triggers an ack back to the kybernete, for continuous awareness of network state in the unreliable WiFi of live performance.

Selection happens downstream, entirely on the receiver's side — next.

03

Nickelodeon
digitale

Nickelodeon digitale

  • Early-cinema nickelodeons: storefront theatres, live musicians improvising accompaniment to silent film
  • Altman's "living" performance space — music as variable, locally specific, never fixed in advance
  • Digitale — digital, but also "of the finger": typing as the project's central performative gesture

Bilderatlas Spring Break

  • A Warburgian Bilderatlas — an atlas of images — against the incongruity of spring break
  • Three acts, ~20 min each — Ieri, Oggi, Domani — a non-linear history of humanity
  • Found footage, Internet Archive & Wikimedia Commons — original audio entirely removed

Arto Fantasma

  • A collective active since 2018, specialising in live sonorization of audiovisual material
  • Clarinet (Edmondo Tedesco), saxophone (Simone Garino), drums (Dario Bruna), electric guitar (Carlo Barbagallo), electric bass (Andrea Valle), double bass (Federico Marchesano) — a groove-and-noise language that Armillaria destabilises and redirects live
fig. Bilderatlas Spring Break — Arto Fantasma, RKH Studio, Turin, 7 May 2026 · video: youtube.com/watch?v=ZhikoQiAcqA
im-prompt-u

The kybernete does not program the music; the kybernete orients a generative device made up of natural agents — musicians who hear, feel, decide, misremember, and productively ignore.

cue sheet Excerpt from Žižek in conferenza (Domani) — timecode, addressee, instruction

A typology of instructions

  • Scene-setters — opening harmonic/affective orientation
  • Instrument roles — selective, one musician at a time
  • Dramatic redirects & juxtaposition prompts
    "Keep smiling while the music becomes slightly inhuman" — "cute pop over body horror"
  • Negative constraints, transitions, stop/cut
    "Do not climax" — "prepare for violent media intrusion" — "Stop. Leave a short, uncomfortable silence."
04

Conclusions

what remains

The gap between what is typed and what is played is not noise to be minimised — it is the compositional substance of the work.
Armillaria — a network and a browser, nothing more

Open directions

  • Stroma — peer-to-peer variant, every node sends and receives, no fixed kybernete
  • An ethnography of the interpretive gap — how performers read, interpret, productively misread
